messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — canary v2-14-7 running in eu-west1 shows a small fastpath p95 bump on short-seq runs. Not sure if it's noise. Snapshot from today: p95 +18ms, p99 +5ms, tail unchanged. Anyone else seeing this?
Liam: Seeing same in eu-west1 canary profiles. Reproduced locally on staging with n=200. Feels consistent across hosts.
Sara: Can you paste the perf/bench command and a tiny metric snippet? Any recent allocator/kernel changes on those images?
Maya: Command I ran: `make bench MODEL=v2-14-quantized FASTPATH=1 N=200 SHORTSEQ=1`
Metrics paste: `p50 12ms, p95 78ms (baseline 60ms), p99 220ms (baseline 215ms)`. Flame quickly showed spikes during KV cache refill.
devops-bot: Deployment note — canary progressed 5% -> 10% at 2468122000. Metric exporter v2.3.1. No crashes.
Liam: Suggest doing a perf record on the worker that showed the spike: `perf record -g -F 99 -o /tmp/perf.data -- ./serve_bench --model v2-14 --seq 64 --runs 200` then `python3 tools/kv_profile.py /tmp/perf.data` to get function-level breakdown.
Maya: Running that perf now on worker-2, ETA ~12m.
Alex: Quick FYI — there was a libc upgrade in the host image last week (glibc 2.36 -> 2.37). Could change small-allocation behavior.
Sara: If alloc churn is the issue, try setting `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libjemalloc.so.2` or `MALLOC_CONF=metadata_thp:0` on a single host to isolate.
Maya: Perf result (short): `hot: realloc ~22% CPU, kv_cache_fill ~40% on worker-2`. Stack traces point to short-lived small allocations during refill.
Liam: That matches hypothesis — quantized decode path seems to allocate more intermediate buffers on refill path. Could be a regression from the newer memory pools.
Sara: Ops proposal: revert canary back to 5% and deploy jemalloc preload image on a small subset to see impact. Vote: react :+1: to revert & patch, :thumbsdown: to continue rollout.
Maya: +1
Liam: +1
Alex: +1 — I'll build a jemalloc-preload image and a quick runbook.
oncall-bot: Action logged — canary reduced to 5% at 2468123300 by Maya. Incident ticket INF-4307 created.
Maya: I'll re-run bench with jemalloc preload and post results here. If p95 delta drops below ~10ms we can continue rollout, otherwise we'll keep the hold and escalate.
devops-bot: Reminder: canary window closes in ~3h. Alert rule: p95 delta > +20ms will auto-pause further rollout.
